summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Everton's 4-1-4-1 (4 changes from the Nott'm Forest game).
Everton created the better chances (1.11 xG to 0.69); Spurs were fortunate to draw.

Compared with their other league games, Spurs got into the box more (39 vs 28), pressed less intensely (5.5 vs 4.1), settled for lower-quality chances (0.05 vs 0.08), went long less often (2.5% vs 3.7%).
Tonali was the biggest attacking threat (0.40 xG + xA); Gray won the ball back most often (4 tackles won + interceptions).

read: Spurs had 62% of the ball (season average 61%), completing 599 of 644 passes (93%).
76% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), above their usual 67%. They spent long spells camped in Everton's half.
32% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (192 own half, 407 opposition half): most of the passing happened high up the pitch.
Long balls made up 2.5% of accurate passes (below the season's 3.7%), with 60% of long balls finding a teammate. Spurs built short and rarely went direct.

Where the xG came from: open play 0.46 (72%), fast breaks 0.00, set pieces 0.18. 9 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).
